question:
(i) Derive the expression for fringe width in Young’s double-slit experiment.
(ii) Light of wavelength $500\,\text{nm}$ is incident on a metal surface of work function $2.0\,\text{eV}$. Calculate the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons in eV. Take $h=6.63\times10^{-34}\,\text{J s}$, $c=3\times10^8\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ and $1\,\text{eV}=1.6\times10^{-19}\,\text{J}$.

options.A:
(i) The fringe width is $\beta=\dfrac{dD}{\lambda}$.
(ii) Photon energy is $2.49\,\text{eV}$ and $K_{\max}=2.0\,\text{eV}$.
options.B:
(i) The fringe width is $\beta=\dfrac{\lambda d}{D}$.
(ii) Photon energy is $0.49\,\text{eV}$, so no photoelectrons are emitted.
options.C:
(i) The fringe width is independent of wavelength.
(ii) $K_{\max}=\phi_0-\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}=-0.49\,\text{eV}$.
options.D:
(i) In YDSE, $\Delta x=\dfrac{dy}{D}$ and for bright fringes $\Delta x=n\lambda$, so $y_n=\dfrac{n\lambda D}{d}$. Hence $\beta=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$.
(ii) $E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}=2.49\,\text{eV}$ and $K_{\max}=E-\phi_0=2.49-2.0=0.49\,\text{eV}$.
